full_judgment:
6. When the suits proceeded on these pleadings, Tamijul Haque, the plaintiff, filed an application before the S.C.C. Court under Order 6, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure. In that application it was alleged that after filing of the suit the plaintiff No. 1 had been diligently pursuing the suit but very recently plaintiff No. 3, namely, Shamsul Haque, his brother, has turned hostile towards the other plain-tiffs and Shamsul Haque has cancelled the power which he gave to the plaintiff No. 1 and hence for the ends of justice and proper adjudication of the suits it became necessary that the name of the plain-tiff Shamsul Haque be struck off from the list of the plaintiffs and the plaint be amended accordingly but as the suit is required to be disposed of in presence of Shamsul Haque his name should be transposed as defendant in the above suits. Vide Order dated 4.9.84 the petition was allowed and it was ordered that the plaintiff No. 3 be transposed as proforma defendant and necessary amendments made and 13.11.84 was fixed for requisites. The plaintiff filed requisites. Thereafter, it was ordered that the summons be is-sued upon the proforma defendant. When that was the case, on 2.1.1985 Shamsul Haque describing himself as plaintiff and proform defendant filed an-other power through another lawyer and submitted a compromise petition stating that the landlord and the tenants have come to a compromise and the solenama has been effected in this regard and the suit therefore be dismissed for non-prosecution in terms of the solenama and the Court was pleased to dismiss the suit for non-prosecution in terms of the solenama. The said order was passed on all the 52 S. C. C. Cases filed by Tamijul Haque against the tenants. Against these orders passed 52 Civil Revisional applications were moved by Mr. Tamijul Haque and these are numbered as Civil Revision Nos. 170-204, 206-222 of 1985. 

 13. In the instant case certain facts are admitted, namely, that at the time when Tamijul Haque instituted the S.C.C. Suits being fifty- seven (57) suits before the learned Munsif and 15 suits before the learned Subordinate Judge against the respective tenants for eviction on the ground of default of payment of rent, Mr. Tamijul Haque filed for himself and for all the plaintiffs which included his two other brothers and heirs of his late brother Azizul Haque and other family members. The plaint of those suits were verified by Mr. Tamijul Haque and every page was signed by Tamijul Haque under a seal which describes him as a constituted attorney for Anwarul Haque, Shamsul Haque, Hakima Khatun, Sadrunnessa, Sajeda Khatun, Ayesha Khatun, Enamul Haque, Ainul Haque, Noor-e-Afshan, Husn-e-Afshan. The plaint was signed by Tamijul Haque as the plaintiff. He executed power in favour of Advocates Mr. Khondker Nurul Islam, Abdul Mannan Talukdar and Giasuddin Chowdhury. It is on record that the tenants in those cases appeared by filing written statements denying the material allegations made therein, On 10th July, 1984 an application by Tamijul Haque was moved before the Court under Order 6, rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure with a copy given to the lawyers for the defendants, who received the copy with objection, wherein it was alleged that very recently the plaintiff No. 3 has turned hostile towards the other plaintiffs and has cancelled the power which he gave to the plaintiff No. 1, so it is necessary that the name of plaintiff No. 3 be struck off from the list of plaintiffs and he be transposed as proforma defendant. From the order sheet it appears that this application was heard on 4.9.84. On the day the defendant filed hazira, petition dated 12.4.84 was put up for hearing and it was ordered by the Court that the petition be allowed and was ordered that the plaintiff No. 3 be transposed as proforma defendant fixing 13.11.84 for requisites. On 13.11.84 the defendant filed hazira. Plaintiffs filed requisities and it was ordered that the summons be issued upon the proforma defendant and 15.12.84 was fixed for service return. Service having not returned, 15.1.85 was fixed for the same. On 2.1.85 Shamsul Haque appeared through a different lawyer with a solenama praying that the suit be dismissed for non-a prosecution on the basis of solenama. An examination of the said solenama filed in Court on 31st December, 1984 by Shamsul Haque for himself and as constituted attorney of Mr. Tamijul Haque, Anwarul Haque, Ayesha Khatun, and others did not show that any copy of the said application was served on the plaintiff Tamijul Haque who instituted those suits before the Court and not also on his lawyer at any point of time. From an examination of the Vokalanama it is seen that Shamsul Haque appeared for the first time in those suits on 2.1.85 instituted originally on 11.5.83 by his brother Tamijul Haque against their common tenants of the Haque Market, by executing a Vokalatnama describing himself as "plaintiff and proforma defendant" by authorising Mr. Ahsanuddin Ahmed, Advocate, to appear on his behalf. It also appears from records that a notice had been issued by the Court upon Mr. Shamsul Haque as a proforma defendant, asking him to appear and re-ply in the suit within 15.12.84. So, it appears that Shamsul Haque had knowledge that his name has been struck off and he had been transposed from plaintiff to the position of a proforma defendant. This order of transposition had not been challenged and that being so it is not understood as to why the learned Munsif failed to take into consideration the fact that Shamsul Haque cannot appear in this case as a plaintiff for recording an order of dismissal for non-prosecution when the other plaintiffs were neither informed nor present: nor there is any evidence to show that they had consented to the compromise. Moreover, Shamsul Haque being only a proforma defendant in the suit cannot possibly make a compromise with other defendants and withdraw from prosecution as a mere compromise between the defendants would not non suit the plaintiff. 

 14. Under the provision of Order 23, rule, sub-rule (4) of the Code of Civil Procedure only one plaintiff cannot withdraw a suit without the consent of other plaintiffs. In the instant case though the plaint was verified by Tamijul Haque on behalf of himself and all others by virtue of a power of attorney, all others were independently named as plaintiffs, therefore, the provision of Order 23, sub-rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure would apply and the order passed allowing the suit to be dismissed for non-prosecution on the basis of solenama, on the application of one proforma defendant plaintiff, would be hit by the provisions of Order 23, rule 1, sub-rule 4.
